title: Compliance Forms, Certifications, and Quote-Submission Procedure
capability_statement: Parsons routinely prepares and submits the full slate of state-procurement compliance forms and certifications that bid solicitations require, and we have done so on prior procurements for comparable Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance (I/M) and motor-vehicle programs. On a recent comparable Emissions Program Management procurement, our proposal explicitly stated that all information submitted pertained exclusively to the proposing Parsons subsidiary, that the proposal satisfied all mandatory requirements listed in the RFP, that we took no exceptions to any of the contractual provisions, and that the signing officer was authorized to bind the corporation to all proposal provisions and acknowledged receipt of all addenda - the same posture this Bid Solicitation requires of bidders submitting through the State eProcurement system (chunk 1928). Our proposals are organized to deliver each required attachment - including PCI-DSS compliance attestations, SOC 2 Type II reports, Accessibility Conformance Reports (Section 508 / WCAG), security testing results, and security incident response plans - as discrete, electronically uploaded files keyed to the procurement's submission structure (chunk 1961), demonstrating fluency with the kind of attachment-by-attachment compliance-package assembly this theme requires. Most of the 148 requirements in this theme, however, are direct procurement-form submissions (Ownership Disclosure, MacBride Principles, Disclosure of Investment Activities in Iran, Disclosure of Investigations, Anti-Discrimination/EEO acknowledgements, Confidentiality and Commitment to Defend, Business Registration Certificate, set-aside acknowledgements, Source Disclosure, Two-Year Chapter 51/Executive Order 117 Certification and Disclosure of Political Contributions, Subcontractor Utilization, MWBE/SBE/VBE certifications) and procedural acknowledgements (submission via the State eProcurement system, Q&A only via the system's Q&A tab, no arbitration, comply-with-all-applicable-laws, exceptions to State Standard Terms and Conditions, mobilization plan with Quote, draft CIF Network and Lane Configuration Plan with Quote, written information security policies and standards with the Third-Party Information Security Questionnaire, performance security with bid where required). For these items the proposal team must execute the form itself, sign as the authorized officer, and attach the supporting documentation - past-performance citation does not substitute for execution. Parsons' company posture supports this directly: as a global, 18,000+-person company with 79 years of experience and audited financial statements (chunks 1975, 2017), we hold the corporate documentation typically required for Ownership Disclosure (10%-or-greater owners, publicly-traded-parent SEC linkage), Business Registration, financial-capability submissions, and continuing-obligation certifications (Iran disclosure, MacBride, Disclosure of Investigations) over the contract term. Our compliance program for prior I/M procurements has been delivered with no exceptions taken to RFP contractual provisions (chunk 1928), an authorized binding signature, and full acknowledgement of all addenda - the standard pattern this Bid Solicitation requires.

differentiators: (1) Demonstrated 'no exceptions taken' posture on a comparable I/M procurement - signed by an officer authorized to bind the corporation, with all addenda acknowledged - exactly mirroring the compliance posture this Bid Solicitation requires of its quote submission (chunk 1928). (2) Existing, organized compliance-attachment template - PCI-DSS, SOC 2 Type II, ACR (Section 508 / WCAG), security testing results, security incident response plan, escrow agreements, disaster recovery plan - already structured as discrete, electronically uploaded files keyed to a state procurement's submission structure (chunk 1961), reducing risk of incomplete or out-of-order submission. (3) Corporate documentation depth: publicly held entity with three years of audited financial statements, credit reference letter, Dun & Bradstreet comprehensive report, employee stock ownership trust ownership profile (more than 60% owned by Parsons Employee Stock Ownership Trust), and a known parent/subsidiary structure that supports both the Ownership Disclosure 10%-or-greater owner question and the publicly-traded-parent SEC-link question without ambiguity (chunks 1975, 2017). (4) Standing diverse-business teaming relationships (SDB, SB, VBE partners with named scopes and multi-year history as Parsons subcontractors), supporting the set-aside acknowledgement and Subcontractor Utilization Plan with credible, contractually committed partners rather than placeholder commitments (chunks 1928, 2007, 2012). (5) Dedicated proposal-management discipline that tracks continuing-obligation certifications (Iran disclosure, MacBride, Disclosure of Investigations) for change-notification updates from the date of certification through contract completion - the type of post-award compliance hygiene this theme expects. (6) Authorized binding-signature and addenda-acknowledgement practice already in place at the corporate-officer level (chunk 1928), eliminating last-minute escalation for proposal sign-off.
gap_notes:
MOST OF THIS THEME IS DIRECT FORM EXECUTION, NOT A CAPABILITY CLAIM. The capture/proposal team must source, complete, sign, and attach the actual forms and supporting documents listed below. Past-performance evidence does not substitute for execution; the listed forms must be provided directly by Parsons' contracts/legal/HR/finance functions:

(a) Ownership Disclosure Form (Q1 non-profit indicator, Q3 corporate/partnership/LLC indicator, Q4 list of 10%-or-greater individual/entity owners with names and addresses, Q6 publicly-traded indicator, Q7 publicly-traded-parent disclosure with SEC-filing link and 10%-or-greater beneficial owners) - Parsons' corporate-secretary function must furnish current cap-table data and SEC-filing links for any publicly-traded parent.

(b) MacBride Principles Form - check one of two boxes (no Northern Ireland operations, or lawful good-faith Northern Ireland operations under MacBride) and provide continuing-obligation acknowledgement.

(c) Disclosure of Investment Activities in Iran Form - certification, with detailed precise description if unable to certify; continuing-obligation acknowledgement; acknowledgement of criminal liability for false statements.

(d) Disclosure of Investigations Form - Part 2 Q1-Q5 (criminal/disorderly arrests/charges/indictments/convictions; suspensions/debarments/ineligibility; pending criminal/debarment proceedings; denied/revoked licenses/permits; adverse public-sector civil litigation in past five years), Part 3 detailed YES-answer descriptions including Person/Entity Name, Contact Name, Phone Number, Case Caption, Investigation Inception, Current Status, and Summary; continuing-obligation acknowledgement.

(e) Anti-Discrimination / EEO acknowledgements per N.J.S.A. 10:2-1 through 10:2-4, N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq., N.J.S.A. 10:5-31 through 10:5-38 - direct acknowledgement; capture team should confirm with HR/Legal that the affirmative-action program documentation is current.

(f) Confidentiality and Commitment to Defend - select one of two options (no confidential/proprietary/trade-secret material with no redactions OR confidential material with detailed statement attached identifying exempt sections); the proposal team must coordinate with technical authors to identify any redacted sections in advance.

(g) Business Registration Certificate (BRC) - capture team must furnish the current New Jersey BRC for Parsons and for each named subcontractor.

(h) Source Disclosure / Two-Year Chapter 51 / Executive Order 117 Certification and Disclosure of Political Contributions - completion by Parsons' compliance/legal function with current disclosable-contribution data.

(i) Set-Aside / Subcontractor Utilization acknowledgements (R-006 at Section 7.1) - direct acknowledgement; SDB/SB/VBE/MWBE/Labor-Surplus firm participation already supported by Parsons' standing teaming relationships (chunks 2002, 2007, 2012).

(j) Quote-Submission procedural items (submit Quotes through the State eProcurement system per A-001 at Section 1; questions only via the Q&A Tab per R-006 at Section 2.1; Quote per Quote Submission Requirements per R-079 at Section 3.1; submit on time addressing all mandatory requirements per R-017 at Section 3) - direct compliance steps for the proposal-management team; no past-performance citation required.

(k) Mobilization Plan with Quote (R-045 at Section 3.18, beginning with date of notification of Contract award and lasting no longer than two weeks) - the proposal team must draft and include this plan; while Parsons' transition-management practice on prior I/M procurements is described as no-transition-risk with in-place teams (chunks 1928, 2006), the specific two-week post-award Mobilization Plan must be authored.

(l) Draft CIF Network and Lane Configuration Plan with Quote (R-054 at Section 3.19) - requires technical/operations content drafted by the proposal team, with the final due Start + 60 days.

(m) Performance Security (R-050 at Section 6.5; R-055 at Section 6.8 - submit with bid in the amount listed in the scope of work, per N.J.A.C. 17:12-2.5) - the proposal team must obtain and submit the bid bond / performance security in the form and amount specified.

(n) Insurance certificates and forms (R-015 Commercial General Liability $1,000,000 per occurrence at 4.2.a; R-026 Professional Liability minimum $1,000,000 in State-approved form at 4.2.d; A-001 Errors & Omissions / Professional Liability / Malpractice at 7.2.1; A-004 Cyber Breach Insurance at 7.2.2; R-040 Cyber Breach Insurance at least $2,000,000 in State-approved policy form at 9.3.E) - capture team must source current Certificates of Insurance and any State-approved policy-form endorsements; the evidence set does not contain the policies themselves.

(o) Third-Party Information Security Questionnaire - mandatory at NDA Recitals (R-003) and Instructions (R-012); requires Section I sponsor information (R-018), Section V written information security policies and standards (A-021), and supporting documentation. Parsons' SOC 2 Type II report (referenced on a comparable procurement at chunk 1961 as Attachment G) and PCI-DSS attestations are available, but the questionnaire itself must be completed by Parsons' Information Security and CISO functions.

(p) Exceptions to State Standard Terms and Conditions (SSTC, R-076 at Section 2.2) - Parsons' practice on a comparable I/M procurement was 'no exceptions taken' (chunk 1928); legal team must confirm whether the same posture is achievable for this Bid Solicitation or whether any exceptions must be filed.

(q) Continuing-obligation post-award updates - Parsons' compliance-management function must track changes to Disclosure of Investigations, Iran certification, and MacBride certification through completion of the contract and notify the State in writing of any changes.

(r) Information-security mandatory acknowledgements scattered through this theme (A-001 at 1.0 maintain responsibility for information security; A-047 at 13.1 endpoint device protection; A-038 at 6.1 PII safeguards; A-076 at 6.10.B third-party due diligence; A-042 at 6.2 privacy program description; A-052 at 9.1 media and cryptographic protection; R-006 at 22.1 vulnerability/patch management; R-046 at 26.1 capacity/performance planning; A-024 at 6.5.B HIPAA/IRS Pub 1075/DPPA/Identity Theft Prevention Act compliance; A-026 at 6.5.C user-information safeguards; A-042 at 6.5.H minimum-necessary State Data; A-043 at 6.5.I State Data return on termination; R-010 at 9.1.5.a orderly return and disposal of State Data on termination; R-003 at 9.1.4.a Security Incident updates; R-025 at 9.1.10 30-day advance notice of upgrades) - these are Information Security commitments that the proposal team must affirm via the security questionnaire and policy-and-standards submission; capability statements should be drawn from Parsons' information-security organization rather than this theme's evidence set.

(s) Federal flow-down provisions (R-013 Solid Waste Disposal Act / RCRA at 7.3; R-019 EPA CPG reference at 7.3.ii; R-031 enforcement action on subcontracts at 7.4(8); R-046 37 CFR Part 401 at 7.8; A-003 Clean Air Act flow-down to subcontracts over $150,000 at 7.9.1.3; A-006 Water Pollution Control Act flow-down to subcontracts over $150,000 at 7.9.2.3) - subcontract-template provisions to be incorporated by Parsons' contracts/legal function; no past-performance citation required.

(t) Collective-bargaining-agreement Exhibits A and B (Dues Authorization and COPE Authorization, M-015 / A-017 / M-016 at Article III) plus Article III, IV, VI, XXIX, XXX, XXXI, and XXXV operational clauses - these are CBA-driven obligations that bind the operating contractor post-award; the proposal team should acknowledge that successor-and-assigns CBA obligations will be honored, but no past-performance evidence in this theme's chunk set substantiates Parsons' specific CBA-administration practice for the bargaining unit at issue.

(u) Voice and naming: per instructions, all references to specific past-performance jurisdictions remain neutralized in the synthesized capability statement (no references to specific contracting agencies' identifiers reintroduced). Where evidence chunks reference specific named jurisdictions or agencies, the synthesized text uses neutral phrasing such as 'comparable State DOT Emissions Program Management procurement,' 'comparable State I/M Program,' or 'a recent comparable procurement.'

HONEST FRAMING: This theme is largely procedural and form-based. Parsons' differentiator here is operational discipline (proposal-management practice, no-exceptions posture on prior procurements, organized compliance-attachment package, standing diverse-business teaming, corporate documentation depth) - not a unique technical capability. Authors should resist over-claiming and should explicitly call out for capture team review the items in (a)-(t) above that require direct execution.
